name: blanks
title: String of Blank Characters
description: Create a string of n blank characters.
case: Five spaces.
done: n spaces, with n floored.

name: deblank
title: Strip Trailing Blanks
description: Remove trailing whitespace from each string.
case: Trailing spaces on one string.
done: Trailing whitespace is removed and the start is kept.

name: strcat
title: Concatenate Strings
description: Paste strings, recycling the second argument once per element of the first.
case: Two pairs pasted with an empty separator.
done: rep(s1, each=length(s2)) pasted onto s2.

name: strcmp
title: Compare Strings
description: TRUE when two character vectors are the same length and equal elementwise.
case: Two equal character vectors, returned as 1.
done: all(s1 == s2) when the lengths match, otherwise FALSE.

name: strcmpi
title: Compare Strings Ignoring Case
description: Case-insensitive strcmp.
case: Ab and aB, returned as 1.
done: strcmp of the lower-case strings.

name: strjust
title: Justify Strings
description: Trim each string and pad it to the widest one.
case: Center a short string beside bb.
done: A unique prefix of left, right, or center. The extra center space goes on the right.

name: strRep
title: Replace a Literal Substring
description: Replace every occurrence of a literal substring.
case: Dots become dashes.
done: gsub with fixed=TRUE.

name: strTrim
title: Trim Whitespace
description: Remove whitespace from both ends.
case: Spaces around one word.
done: Leading and trailing whitespace.

name: refindall
title: Find Every Match
description: 1-based starts of a Perl pattern, stepping by over after each hit.
case: Overlapping aba in ababab.
done: The next search starts at the match plus over.

name: regexp
title: Match Regular Expression
description: Starts, ends, and text of Perl matches in the first string.
case: Starts of ab in abcabc.
done: gregexpr unless once is TRUE. No match returns None.

name: regexpi
title: Match Ignoring Case
description: regexp with ignorecase TRUE.
case: Both a's in Aa.
done: The same list as regexp.

name: regexprep
title: Replace with a Regular Expression
description: Replace matches of a Perl pattern.
case: ab replaced ignoring case.
done: gsub, or sub when once is TRUE.

name: cd
title: Change Directory
description: Change the process working directory and return it.
case: Change to /tmp, compare the real path, and change back. Both sides return 1.
done: os.chdir. With no argument, return the current directory.
r: { old <- getwd(); cd("/tmp"); ok <- as.numeric(normalizePath(pwd(), winslash="/") == normalizePath("/tmp", winslash="/")); setwd(old); ok }

name: clear
title: Remove Workspace Names
description: Remove names from the module workspace.
case: Create zz_pracma, remove that one name, and return 1.
done: A missing argument clears the workspace dict. It does not touch process globals.
r: { assign("zz_pracma", 1, envir=globalenv()); clear("zz_pracma"); as.numeric(!exists("zz_pracma", envir=globalenv(), inherits=FALSE)) }
py: (lambda s=__import__("pracma.util_session", fromlist=["workspace"]): (s.workspace.__setitem__("zz_pracma", 1), clear("zz_pracma"), 1.0 if "zz_pracma" not in s.workspace else 0.0)[2])()

name: pwd
title: Working Directory
description: Return the process working directory.
case: pwd matches the current directory. Both sides return 1.
done: os.getcwd.

name: what
title: List Files
description: Print the files in a directory and return None.
case: A missing directory returns None.
done: Prints the message and returns None.

name: who
title: List Workspace Names
description: Sorted names in the module workspace.
case: zz_pracma is present, then removed. Both sides return 1.
done: Reads the module dict, sorted like ls().
r: { assign("zz_pracma", 1, envir=globalenv()); ans <- as.numeric("zz_pracma" %in% who()); rm(list="zz_pracma", envir=globalenv()); ans }
py: (lambda s=__import__("pracma.util_session", fromlist=["workspace"]): (s.workspace.__setitem__("zz_pracma", 1), 1.0 if "zz_pracma" in who() else 0.0, s.workspace.pop("zz_pracma", None))[1])()

name: whos
title: Describe Workspace Names
description: Print a line for each workspace name and return the names.
case: zz_pracma is among the names, then removed. Both sides return 1.
done: An empty workspace returns None.
r: { zz_pracma <- 1; res <- NULL; invisible(capture.output(res <- whos())); ans <- as.numeric("zz_pracma" %in% res); rm(zz_pracma); ans }
py: (lambda s=__import__("pracma.util_session", fromlist=["workspace"]): (s.workspace.__setitem__("zz_pracma", 1), 1.0 if "zz_pracma" in (whos() or []) else 0.0, s.workspace.pop("zz_pracma", None))[1])()

name: rand
title: Uniform Random Matrix
description: A matrix of uniform draws on [0, 1).
case: Shape 2 by 4 and 1 when every entry is in [0, 1).
done: runif filled down the columns. A length-2 n sets both dimensions.
py: (lambda x=rand(2, 4): np.concatenate([np.array(x.shape, float), [1.0 if np.all((x >= 0) & (x < 1)) else 0.0]]))()

name: randn
title: Normal Random Matrix
description: A matrix of standard normal draws.
case: Shape 3 by 2 and 1 when every entry is finite.
done: rnorm. The same shape rules as rand.
py: (lambda x=randn(3, 2): np.concatenate([np.array(x.shape, float), [1.0 if np.all(np.isfinite(x)) else 0.0]]))()

name: randi
title: Random Integers
description: Integers from imin to imax, inclusive.
case: Shape 3 by 4 and 1 when every entry is an integer from 2 to 5.
done: A scalar imax starts at 1.
r: { x <- randi(c(2, 5), 3, 4); c(dim(x), as.numeric(all(x >= 2 & x <= 5 & x == floor(x)))) }
py: (lambda x=randi([2, 5], 3, 4): np.concatenate([np.array(x.shape, float), [1.0 if np.all((x >= 2) & (x <= 5) & (x == np.floor(x))) else 0.0]]))()

name: randp
title: Random Points in a Disk
description: Uniform points in a disk of radius r.
case: Shape n by 2 and 1 when every radius is at most r.
done: The radius uses one uniform and two normals.
py: (lambda x=randp(6, 2): (lambda rad=np.sqrt(np.sum(x**2, axis=1)): np.concatenate([np.array(x.shape, float), [1.0 if np.all(rad <= 2 + 1e-8) else 0.0]]))())()

name: rands
title: Random Points on a Sphere
description: Rows of length r on a sphere in N+1 dimensions.
case: Shape 5 by 3 and 1 when every row has length 3.
done: Normalize rows of a normal matrix.
r: { x <- rands(5, N=2, r=3); c(dim(x), as.numeric(all(abs(sqrt(rowSums(x^2)) - 3) < 1e-8))) }
py: (lambda x=rands(5, N=2, r=3): (lambda rad=np.sqrt(np.sum(x**2, axis=1)): np.concatenate([np.array(x.shape, float), [1.0 if np.all(np.abs(rad - 3) < 1e-8) else 0.0]]))())()

name: randsample
title: Random Sample
description: Sample k values from 1:n, or from a numeric vector.
case: Length 4 and 1 when the values are a subset of 1:10.
done: A weight vector forces replacement.
r: { x <- randsample(10, 4); c(length(x), as.numeric(all(x >= 1 & x <= 10) && length(unique(x)) == 4)) }
py: (lambda x=randsample(10, 4): np.array([float(np.size(x)), 1.0 if np.all((x >= 1) & (x <= 10)) and len(set(np.asarray(x).tolist())) == 4 else 0.0]))()

name: matlab
title: Matlab Compatibility
description: Print the list of Matlab-style names and return None.
case: The call returns None.
done: The printed list is the source text.

name: beep
title: Beep
description: Write the bell character and return None.
case: The call returns None.
done: cat of the bell character.

name: disp
title: Display
description: Print arguments and a newline, then return None.
case: disp of one word returns None.
done: print with a trailing newline.

name: ver
title: Version Banner
description: Print a version banner and return None.
case: The call returns None.
done: The banner uses the Python version and platform.

name: isempty
title: Empty Object
description: TRUE when the object has length zero.
case: An empty vector is 1 and a zero is 0.
done: length(x) == 0. A scalar is not empty.
py: np.array([1.0 if isempty([]) else 0.0, 1.0 if isempty(0) else 0.0])

name: ndims
title: Number of Dimensions
description: 0 for an empty object, 1 for a vector, otherwise the rank.
case: A vector, a matrix, and an empty vector.
done: A matrix is 2 even though size reports 1 by n for a vector.

name: nnz
title: Nonzero Count
description: How many entries are not zero.
case: Two nonzeros in a length-4 vector.
done: Complex values count as nonzero when either part is.

name: numel
title: Number of Elements
description: Product of the size vector.
case: A vector, a 2 by 3 matrix, and an empty vector.
done: A vector of length 5 has size 1 by 5, so numel is 5.

name: size
title: Size of an Array
description: 1 by n for a vector, otherwise the dimension vector.
case: A length-5 vector and a 2 by 3 matrix.
done: k past the rank returns 1. k below 1 is an error.

name: num2str
title: Format Numbers
description: sprintf of a number, keeping a matrix shape.
case: Two numbers with two digits, joined by a bar.
done: A numeric fmt becomes %.<digits>f.

name: str2num
title: Parse a Matrix String
description: Read a Matlab-style matrix from text.
case: The matrix [1, 2; 3, 4] with printing suppressed.
done: A trailing semicolon skips the print. An empty parse is None.

name: findstr
title: Find the Shorter String
description: 1-based starts of the shorter string in the longer one.
case: abc searched in ab, which swaps and finds position 1.
done: An empty pattern is None.

name: strfind
title: Find a Substring
description: 1-based starts of pattern s2 in each string.
case: ab in abxab.
done: One string returns a vector. Several strings return a list.

name: strfindi
title: Find a Substring Ignoring Case
description: strfind after lower-casing both sides.
case: AB in AbXab.
done: Same positions as strfind.

name: figure
title: Control Plot Devices
description: Check a figure handle, or open an Agg figure, and return what R returns.
case: figure() returns None. Handles 0 and 1 raise the R errors.
done: No X11 window. Device 1 is the null device. Handle 0 is in use.
r: { old <- getwd(); setwd(tempdir()); figure(); while (dev.cur() > 1) dev.off(); setwd(old); NULL }

name: tic
title: Start a Timer
description: Store the current performance counter.
case: tic then toc is a nonnegative number, returned as 1.
done: One toc reads the stored time.

name: toc
title: Read the Timer
description: Seconds since tic. echo prints a line and still returns the number.
case: tic then one toc(echo=False) is nonnegative, returned as 1.
done: The value is the elapsed seconds.

name: fprintf
title: Formatted Printing
description: sprintf the text, write it, and return how many characters were written.
case: The text written for one integer and one two-digit float.
done: The check compares that text, not the character count.
r: { tf <- tempfile(); fprintf("id=%d val=%.2f", 7, 1.25, file=tf); paste(readLines(tf, warn=FALSE), collapse="") }

name: loglog
title: Log-log Plot
description: Plot x and y on logarithmic axes and draw a grid.
case: The plotted y is 1, 2, 3. R time is that series, not a graphics device.
done: Matplotlib draws the line. The function returns None.

name: semilogx
title: Semi-log X Plot
description: Plot with a logarithmic x axis.
case: The plotted y is 1, 2, 3. R time is that series, not a graphics device.
done: Matplotlib draws the line. The function returns None.

name: semilogy
title: Semi-log Y Plot
description: Plot with a logarithmic y axis.
case: The plotted y is 1, 10, 100. R time is that series, not a graphics device.
done: Matplotlib draws the line. The function returns None.

name: plotyy
title: Two Y Axes
description: Plot two series against a shared x, with a second y axis.
usage: plotyy(x1, y1, x2, y2, gridp=TRUE, box_col='grey', type='l', lwd=1, lty=1, xlab='x', ylab='y', main='', col_y1='navy', col_y2='maroon')
case: The two plotted series, squares and square roots. R time is that series, not a graphics device.
done: Matplotlib draws both series. The function returns None.
r: { pdf(file.path(tempdir(), "p.pdf")); x1 <- 1:5; y1 <- x1^2; x2 <- 1:5; y2 <- sqrt(x2); plotyy(x1,y1,x2,y2); dev.off(); c(y1, y2) }
py: (lambda: (plotyy(np.arange(1,6), np.arange(1,6)**2, np.arange(1,6), np.sqrt(np.arange(1,6))), np.array(__import__('pracma.util_plot', fromlist=['_drawn'])._drawn['value'], copy=True))[1])()

name: ezcontour
title: Contour of a Function
description: Evaluate f(c(x, y)) on a linspace grid and draw the contour.
usage: ezcontour(fn, xlim=c(-pi, pi), ylim=c(-pi, pi), n=60, filled=FALSE, col=None)
case: x^2 + y^2 on a 4 by 4 grid. R time is that matrix, not a graphics device.
done: F[i, j] is f at the i-th x and j-th y. The function returns None.
r: { xx <- linspace(0, 1, 4); yy <- linspace(0, 1, 4); F <- matrix(NA, 4, 4); for (i in 1:4) for (j in 1:4) F[i,j] <- xx[i]^2 + yy[j]^2; pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); ezcontour(function(v) v[1]^2+v[2]^2, c(0,1), c(0,1), n=4); dev.off(); as.numeric(F) }
py: (lambda: (ezcontour(lambda v: v[0]**2 + v[1]**2, [0,1], [0,1], n=4), np.array(__import__('pracma.util_plot', fromlist=['_drawn'])._drawn['value'], copy=True))[1])()

name: ezmesh
title: Mesh of a Function
description: Evaluate f on a grid and draw a surface mesh.
usage: ezmesh(fn, xlim=c(-pi, pi), ylim=c(-pi, pi), n=60)
case: The product grid. R time is that matrix, not a graphics device.
done: Matplotlib draws the surface. The function returns None.
r: { xx <- linspace(0, 1, 4); yy <- linspace(0, 1, 4); F <- matrix(NA, 4, 4); for (i in 1:4) for (j in 1:4) F[i,j] <- xx[i]*yy[j]; pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); ezmesh(function(v) v[1]*v[2], c(0,1), c(0,1), n=4); dev.off(); as.numeric(F) }
py: (lambda: (ezmesh(lambda v: v[0]*v[1], [0,1], [0,1], n=4), np.array(__import__('pracma.util_plot', fromlist=['_drawn'])._drawn['value'], copy=True))[1])()

name: ezplot
title: Function Plot
description: Plot f on seq(a, b, length.out=n).
usage: ezplot(fn, a, b, n=101, col='blue', add=FALSE)
case: sin on five points from 0 to pi. R time is that series, not a graphics device.
done: Matplotlib draws the line. The function returns None.
r: { pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); ezplot(sin, 0, pi, n=5); dev.off(); sin(seq(0, pi, length.out=5)) }

name: ezpolar
title: Polar Function Plot
description: Evaluate fun on 91 angles and draw them in polar coordinates.
case: sin from 0 to pi. R time is that radius series, not a graphics device.
done: Matplotlib draws the polar curve. The function returns None.
r: { pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); ezpolar(sin, c(0, pi)); dev.off(); sin(seq(0, pi, length.out=91)) }

name: ezsurf
title: Surface of a Function
description: Evaluate f on a grid and draw a colored surface.
usage: ezsurf(fn, xlim=c(-pi, pi), ylim=c(-pi, pi), n=60)
case: x + y on a 4 by 4 grid. R time is that matrix, not a graphics device.
done: Matplotlib draws the surface. The function returns None.
r: { xx <- linspace(-1, 1, 4); yy <- linspace(-1, 1, 4); F <- matrix(NA, 4, 4); for (i in 1:4) for (j in 1:4) F[i,j] <- xx[i]+yy[j]; pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); ezsurf(function(v) v[1]+v[2], c(-1,1), c(-1,1), n=4); dev.off(); as.numeric(F) }
py: (lambda: (ezsurf(lambda v: v[0]+v[1], [-1,1], [-1,1], n=4), np.array(__import__('pracma.util_plot', fromlist=['_drawn'])._drawn['value'], copy=True))[1])()

name: fplot
title: Plot on an Interval
description: ezplot of f on an interval, with an empty title.
case: sin on 101 points from 0 to 1. R time is that series, not a graphics device.
done: The default length is 101. The function returns None.
r: { pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); fplot(sin, c(0, 1)); dev.off(); sin(seq(0, 1, length.out=101)) }

name: errorbar
title: Error Bars
description: Plot points and symmetric error bars.
usage: errorbar(x, y, xerr=None, yerr=None, bar_col='red', bar_len=0.01, grid=TRUE, with_=TRUE, add=FALSE)
case: y and the ends of the vertical bars. R time is that series, not a graphics device.
done: with_ is R's with. Matplotlib draws the bars. The function returns None.
r: { pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); y <- c(1,2,3,4); yerr <- rep(0.1, 4); errorbar(1:4, y, yerr=yerr); dev.off(); c(y, y-yerr, y+yerr) }

name: andrewsplot
title: Andrews Curves
description: Plot one Andrews curve per row.
case: The curve matrix for a 2 by 2 matrix and five angles. R time is that matrix, not a graphics device.
done: f is an integer vector. style is cart or pol. The function returns None.
r: { A <- matrix(c(1,2,3,4), 2, 2); npts <- 5; xpts <- seq(0, 2*pi, length.out=npts); Y <- matrix(NA, 2, npts); for (i in 1:2) { xs <- A[i,]; ypts <- c(); for (p in xpts) { y <- xs[1]; for (j in 2:2) { if (j %% 2 == 1) y <- y + xs[j]*sin((j %/% 2)*p) else y <- y + xs[j]*cos((j %/% 2)*p) }; ypts <- c(ypts, y) }; Y[i,] <- ypts }; pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); andrewsplot(A, c(1L,2L), style="cart", npts=5); dev.off(); as.numeric(Y) }
py: (lambda: (andrewsplot(np.array([[1.,3.],[2.,4.]]), np.array([1,2]), style="cart", npts=5), np.array(__import__('pracma.util_plot', fromlist=['_drawn'])._drawn['value'], copy=True))[1])()

name: polar
title: Polar Plot
description: Draw polar coordinates in the plane.
usage: polar(t, r, type='l', col='blue', grcol='darkgrey', bxcol='black', main='Polar Plot', add=FALSE)
case: Cartesian x and y of three radii. R time is that series, not a graphics device.
done: x = r cos t and y = r sin t. The function returns None.
r: { t <- c(0, pi/2, pi); r <- c(1,2,1); pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); polar(t, r); dev.off(); as.numeric(cbind(r*cos(t), r*sin(t))) }
py: (lambda: (polar(np.array([0, np.pi/2, np.pi]), np.array([1.,2,1])), np.array(__import__('pracma.util_plot', fromlist=['_drawn'])._drawn['value'], copy=True))[1])()

name: quiver
title: Arrow Plot
description: Draw arrows from (x, y) by scale times (u, v).
usage: quiver(x, y, u, v, scale=0.05, angle=10, length=0.1)
case: The arrow ends. R time is that series, not a graphics device.
done: R needs an open plot. Python opens an Agg figure. The function returns None.
r: { x <- c(0,1); y <- c(0,0); u <- c(1,0); v <- c(0,1); scale <- 0.05; pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); plot(c(0,1), c(0,0.05), type="n"); quiver(x,y,u,v, scale=scale); dev.off(); c(x+scale*u, y+scale*v) }
py: (lambda: (quiver(np.array([0.,1]), np.array([0.,0]), np.array([1.,0]), np.array([0.,1]), scale=0.05), np.array(__import__('pracma.util_plot', fromlist=['_drawn'])._drawn['value'], copy=True))[1])()

name: vectorfield
title: Vector Field
description: Evaluate a field on a mesh and draw it with quiver.
usage: vectorfield(fun, xlim, ylim, n=16, scale=0.05, col='green')
case: x + y on a 4 by 4 mesh. R time is that matrix, not a graphics device.
done: The horizontal component is 1. The function returns None.
r: { xpts <- linspace(0, 1, 4); ypts <- linspace(0, 1, 4); M <- meshgrid(xpts, ypts); pdf(file.path(tempdir(),"p.pdf")); vectorfield(function(x,y) x+y, c(0,1), c(0,1), n=4); dev.off(); as.numeric(M$X + M$Y) }
py: (lambda: (vectorfield(lambda x, y: x+y, [0,1], [0,1], n=4), np.array(__import__('pracma.util_plot', fromlist=['_drawn'])._drawn['value'], copy=True))[1])()

name: meshgrid
title: Mesh Grid
description: X holds x across columns and Y holds y down rows.
case: meshgrid of 1:2 and 3:5, X then Y.
done: Same layout as numpy meshgrid.

name: peaks
title: Peaks Surface
description: The Matlab peaks function on a grid or on two vectors.
case: Z for a 3 by 3 grid from -3 to 3.
done: A scalar v builds linspace(-3, 3, v).

name: bits
title: Binary Representation
description: Binary digits of a number by subtracting powers of two.
case: The 54 fractional bits of pi.
done: nextpow2 chooses the integer width, then one step is subtracted when the power overshoots.

name: repmat
title: Replicate a Matrix
description: Tile a matrix with the Kronecker product of a block of ones.
case: A 2 by 2 matrix tiled twice down.
done: A vector is one row. A nonpositive count is a zero matrix.

name: Reshape
title: Reshape Column Major
description: Give an array n rows and m columns, filled down columns.
case: 1:6 as two rows.
done: m defaults to length %/% n. The length must be n*m.

name: sortrows
title: Sort Matrix Rows
description: Order rows by column k, which is 1-based.
case: Three rows ordered by the first column.
done: Ties keep their original order.

name: perms
title: All Permutations
description: Every permutation of a vector, in the pracma order.
case: The six permutations of 10, 20, 30.
done: The index table is built recursively, then applied column-major.

name: randperm
title: Random Permutation
description: A random permutation of 1:n, or a sample of a vector. R is 1-based.
case: Length 7 and 1 when the draw is a permutation of 1:7.
done: A scalar a becomes 1:a. A first element of 0 is empty.
py: (lambda x=randperm(7): np.array([float(np.size(x)), 1.0 if np.array_equal(np.sort(x), np.arange(1, 8)) else 0.0]))()

name: arrayfun
title: Apply to Elements
description: Apply a function to each element and keep the first array's shape.
case: Squares of a 2 by 2 matrix, column-major.
done: Elements are visited down columns.

name: bsxfun
title: Elementwise Binary Function
description: Apply a function to two vectors or two same-size arrays.
case: Add 10 to a 2 by 2 matrix.
done: sweep names MARGIN, so the two matrices are combined elementwise.
py: bsxfun(lambda a, b: a+b, np.array([[1.,3.],[2.,4.]]), np.full((2,2), 10.0))

name: fftshift
title: Swap FFT Halves
description: Move the second half of a vector in front of the first.
case: 1:5 rotated with the longer half first.
done: The split is ceiling(length/2).

name: ifft
title: Inverse FFT
description: Inverse FFT divided by the length, matching pracma.
case: Real part of the inverse of 1, 2, 3, 4.
done: NumPy ifft already divides by n, which is what pracma does after R's unnormalized inverse.

name: ifftshift
title: Inverse FFT Rotation
description: Move the second half in front, splitting at floor(length/2).
case: 1:5 rotated with the shorter half first.
done: The split is floor(length/2).

name: histc
title: Histogram Counts
description: Count values in half-open bins, and put the rightmost edge in the last bin.
case: Counts and bins for seq(0, 1, by=0.05) on tenths from 0.1 to 0.9.
done: edges[i] <= x < edges[i+1], and x == edges[n] is bin n.
py: (lambda x=np.arange(0, 1.0000001, 0.05): (lambda e=np.arange(0.1, 0.9000001, 0.1): (lambda h=histc(x, e): np.concatenate([np.asarray(h["cnt"], float).reshape(-1), np.asarray(h["bin"], float).reshape(-1)]))())())()

name: histss
title: Histogram Bin Width
description: Choose a bin width by the Shimazaki-Shinomoto cost and return the counts.
case: Counts for ten values and n=5.
done: Bins are right-closed, and the lowest bin includes the left edge.

name: ceil
title: Ceiling
description: Round toward positive infinity.
case: Ceiling of -1.2 and 1.2.
done: R ceiling.

name: Fix
title: Truncate toward Zero
description: Drop the fractional part.
case: Truncation of -1.7 and 1.7.
done: R trunc. The name stays Fix.

name: gcd
title: Greatest Common Divisor
description: Extended Euclidean gcd. extended returns g, c, and d.
case: gcd and the two coefficients of (12, 8) and (-8, 12).
done: Coefficients are multiplied by the sign of a.
r: { g <- gcd(c(12, -8), c(8, 12), extended=TRUE); c(g$g, g$c, g$d) }

name: idivide
title: Integer Division
description: Divide integers and round by fix, floor, ceil, or round.
done: A unique prefix selects the mode. An ambiguous prefix is the R match.arg error.

name: Lcm
title: Least Common Multiple
description: a / gcd(a, b) * b.
done: The name stays Lcm. A negative input keeps its sign.

name: mod
title: Modulo
description: Remainder with the sign of the divisor. Zero divisor returns n.
case: mod of -7, 7, and 8 by 3.
done: R %%. m must be an integer scalar.

name: rem
title: Remainder
description: Remainder with the sign of the dividend. Zero divisor is NaN.
case: rem of -7, 7, and 8 by -3.
done: Adjust the modulo result when the signs differ.

name: geomean
title: Geometric Mean
description: exp of the mean of the logs, along a dimension.
case: Column geometric means of a 2 by 3 matrix.
done: dim 1 collapses rows. A vector only allows dim 1.

name: harmmean
title: Harmonic Mean
description: Reciprocal of the mean of the reciprocals.
case: Column harmonic means of a 2 by 3 matrix.
done: dim 1 collapses rows.

name: trimmean
title: Trimmed Mean
description: Mean after dropping round(n * percent/100/2) values from each end.
case: 40 percent trimmed mean of five numbers.
done: A matrix is trimmed down each column.

name: accumarray
title: Accumulate by Index
description: Apply a function to values that share a subscript. Indices are 1-based.
case: Sums of 101:106 at six row-column subscripts.
done: A vector of subscripts stays a vector. A matrix of subscripts is column-major.
r: { val <- 101:106; subs <- matrix(c(1, 2, 1, 2, 3, 1, 4, 1, 4, 4, 4, 1), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE); as.numeric(accumarray(subs, val)) }

name: uniq
title: Unique Values and Indexes
description: Unique values in order of appearance, with the index maps m and n.
case: b, m, and n for 3, 1, 3, 2, 1.
done: m is the last index unless first is TRUE. n is 1-based.

name: distmat
title: Euclidean Distance Matrix
description: Distances between the rows of two matrices.
case: Distances from two points to (0, 1).
done: A vector is one row. Negative roundoff is clamped to zero.
r: { X <- matrix(c(0,0,1,0), 2, 2, byrow=TRUE); Y <- matrix(c(0,1), 1, 2); as.numeric(distmat(X, Y)) }

name: hausdorff_dist
title: Hausdorff Distance
description: The larger of the two directed Hausdorff distances.
case: Two segments a unit apart.
done: max of the row-minima and the column-minima of the distance matrix.
r: { P <- matrix(c(0,0,1,0), 2, 2, byrow=TRUE); Q <- matrix(c(0,1,1,1), 2, 2, byrow=TRUE); hausdorff_dist(P, Q) }

name: pdist
title: Pairwise Distances
description: distmat of a matrix with itself.
case: Pairwise distances of two points.
done: The diagonal is zero.

name: pdist2
title: Distances between Two Sets
description: distmat of two matrices.
case: Distances between two pairs of points.
done: Same values as distmat.
r: { X <- matrix(c(0,0,3,4), 2, 2, byrow=TRUE); Y <- matrix(c(0,0,1,1), 2, 2, byrow=TRUE); as.numeric(pdist2(X, Y)) }
